About Gabe Parent

Experienced, steady, and directly involved.

Gabe Parent is an experienced logger based in St. Albans, Vermont. He operates Parent Timber Harvesting as an owner-operated whole-tree logging business and works directly with landowners, farmers, sugarmakers, foresters, and forest managers.

His reputation is built on careful work, practical judgment, repeat customers, and respect for the land. Gabe primarily works alone, which means landowners and foresters deal directly with the person carrying out the work in the woods.

Parent Timber Harvesting is especially well suited for jobs where experience, water quality protection, careful site handling, and good working relationships matter.

Services

Whole-tree harvesting with field-tested judgment.

Parent Timber Harvesting works on practical timber harvesting jobs where the work needs to fit the land, the landowner’s goals, and the forester’s plan.

1

Whole-tree timber harvesting

Gabe operates a whole-tree harvesting system using skidders, a feller buncher, and a loader, with direct owner involvement from start to finish.

2

Farm woodlot harvesting

Farm woodlots are part of a larger working property. Gabe pays attention to access, fields, fences, soils, drainage, water, and future land use.

3

Sugarbush timber harvesting

Gabe owns a sugarbush himself and understands how to improve the woods while protecting access, maple trees, soils, and long-term productivity.

4

Forester-guided harvests

Parent Timber Harvesting works with consulting foresters, public foresters, forest managers, and landowners to turn harvest plans into careful field work.

5

Forest improvement harvests

Good harvesting is not only about removing timber. It is also about protecting remaining trees and supporting the landowner’s long-term goals.

6

Landing and loader work

Logs are handled, sorted, and loaded with attention to the job, the market, and the condition of the landing and access system.

Farm woodlots and sugarbushes

Care for the whole property.

Farm woodlots and sugarbushes require more than ordinary timber removal. The job has to fit access, drainage, field edges, soils, future maple production, and the landowner’s long-term use of the property.

Gabe Parent brings calm judgment and firsthand experience to this work. He understands that the condition of the land after the job matters as much as the timber harvested from it.

  • Farm access, fields, fences, and soils are treated as part of the job.
  • Sugarbush work is approached with attention to future stand quality and maple productivity.
  • Communication with landowners and foresters stays practical and direct.
Water quality and trust

Known for careful attention to Vermont AMPs.

Parent Timber Harvesting is known for strict attention to Vermont Forestry Acceptable Management Practices for protecting water quality.

Gabe takes care with trail layout, landings, drainage, erosion control, and stream crossings so harvesting is done responsibly and the land is protected.

Water quality

Trails, landings, and crossings are handled with water movement, drainage, and erosion control in mind.

Landowner respect

Gabe treats stumpage payments as a serious responsibility and approaches each job with respect for the landowner.

Repeat relationships

The business has grown through productive work with landowners, farmers, sugarmakers, and foresters.

In the woods

Real work. Real equipment. Real Vermont sites.

The site is built around Gabe’s own photos because the business is grounded in actual field experience, not stock images or generic claims.
